contract.words: Collect $5,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $5,000 of settled cash collected by day 30 with no up-front capital

strategy.title: Sell the $700 ISPM-15 batch-record workbook to 8 more certified pallet facilities from the 1,200 not yet contacted
strategy.why: The price is established by payment-processor records: 26 pallet manufacturers paid $700 each through the offer's checkout link (2026-11). Conversion is measured on this same offer and price: 26 of 200 contacts (13%). The agency's list holds 1,400 certified facilities with contact emails (counted 2026-11-15), 200 already contacted, so 1,200 remain. 8 sales x $700 = $5,600 gross, $5,552 after the $6 direct cost each, covers the $5,000 target; at 13% that needs about 62 contacts, and the plan writes to 120 (expected ~15 sales). Brain produces the workbook itself (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved), no capital is tied up, and cash is usable 4 days after sale, well inside 30 days.

alternatives.title: Write to all 1,200 uncontacted facilities at once
alternatives.why: More headroom (expected ~156 sales) but unnecessary for the target; kept as the fallback if the first 120 convert below plan.

strategy.title: Price-test the ISPM-15 batch-record workbook at $700 on uncontacted certified facilities, then sell 8
strategy.why: The opening's record changed: its price fact now reads "$70" while the card's priceCents is $700, so the price is contradicted and no longer established (the payment-processor record of 26 buyers at $700 is gone from the card). Everything else stands on EVIDENCE: 1,400 certified facilities with contact emails, 200 contacted, 1,200 not; 26 agreements from 200 contacts on this offer; Brain produces the spreadsheet; $6 direct cost; no capital; 4 days to usable cash. A first priced batch at $700 measures the price at no cost. If it holds, 8 x $700 = $5,600 settles by day 12 against the $5,000 target; if buyers only pay $70, the same list still holds enough facilities to re-plan (72 sales needed, about 554 contacts at 13%).

facts.value: The certification agency lists 1,400 ISPM-15 certified facilities with a contact email (counted 2026-11-15); 200 have been contacted. Each needs one workbook.
Sell ISPM-15 heat-treatment batch record workbook for pallet manufacturers to each buyer.

reviews.reasons: Every link of the single member is established by the card's own EVIDENCE facts. Price: 26 pallet manufacturers paid $700 each through this offer's checkout link (payment processor records, 2026-11), a real purchase price from this buyer population, and the card holds one priceCents 70000. Volume: the certification agency lists 1,400 certified facilities with contact email (counted 2026-11-15), 200 contacted, 1,200 not, one workbook each. Conversion 26/200 = 13% measured on the same offer and price. Delivery is a spreadsheet Brain produces (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved); direct cost $6 < $700; exposure $0; 4 days to usable cash. Brain's two failed links contradict the card rather than being contradicted by it: 'no single price on the card' is false (one price, one EVIDENCE price fact), and its 'market holds only 15' figure is the day of the count date (2026-11-15), not the 1,400 the fact states; the author's recorded disagreements cite the specific facts and I agree with both. Arithmetic recomputed: 8 sales needed (7 x $700 = $4,900 < $5,000; 8 x $700 = $5,600); 120 contacts x 13% = 15.6 expected, about 2x the need, with a fallback batch of 200 by day 10 and 1,080 more in reserve; cost 8 x $6 = $48 from receipts, $0 up-front; net $5,552; sales day 3, settled day 7 of 30. EXECUTABLE is right.
findings: Brain's link evaluator appears to read a number out of the count date (2026-11-15 -> 15 buyers) and to reject a price fact that contains several numbers; this card's links should be re-evaluated, after which OFFER_AND_PRICE and MARKET_VOLUME hold.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED: setup before s1, not an evidential gap.
The cash entry settles on day 7 while sales are on day 3 with 4 days to cash: consistent.

reviews.reasons: The opening's record changed: the price fact now reads '$70' while the card's priceCents is $700, and the payment-processor record of 26 buyers paying $700 is gone. Two figures that disagree by 10x on the same card mean the price is contradicted and not established, so EXECUTABLE is no longer supportable and CONDITIONAL with validation.decides = OFFER_AND_PRICE is the right stance; the plan does not treat the price as known (quantity UNKNOWN, source matchesBuyer false). The other links still stand on EVIDENCE: 1,400 listed facilities with contact emails, 1,200 uncontacted (Brain's 'only 15' is still the day of the 2026-11-15 count date, and the recorded disagreement is right); conversion 26/200 = 13% on this offer; Brain-produced spreadsheet; $6 cost; $0 exposure; 4 days to cash. A priced live batch is the correct decisive test: no published comparable would show these buyers paying. Arithmetic recomputed: at $700, 8 sales needed (7 x $700 = $4,900 < $5,000), 8 x $700 = $5,600, net $5,552; proof 4 of 60 by day 6 (6.7%), and at that bare rate the 240-contact second batch adds about 16, so the target is reached by day 12 with margin. At $70 the fallback needs 72 sales (72 x $70 = $5,040; 71 gives $4,970), about 554 contacts at 13%, inside the 1,140 left after the test. $0 capital throughout.
findings: The 13% conversion was measured at an unrecorded price now that the $700 payment record is gone; if those 26 bought at $70, the rate does not predict $700 conversion. The test measures both together, which is fine, but the fallback at $70 should be treated as conversion-measured only if the 26 sales were at $70.

Time risk on the fallback: if the $700 test fails on day 6, the $70 re-plan has 24 days to contact about 554 facilities and settle 72 sales. Running a small $70 arm in parallel with the $700 test (e.g., 30 + 30 contacts) would decide the price in one round instead of two.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED: setup before s1.
